headline: Pittsburgh Water Forgives Utility Debt for Struggling Families
meta_description: Pittsburgh Water's Arrearage Forgiveness Program automatically enrolls 4,300 low-income households and erases outstanding debt over 24 months for those who sta…
summary_short: Pittsburgh Water is forgiving utility debt for nearly 4,300 households living below the poverty line, erasing arrears gradually as families make monthly payments.
body:
Pittsburgh Water has launched a lifeline for families drowning in utility debt: the Arrearage Forgiveness Program, which automatically enrolled approximately 4,300 city households living below 200% of the Federal Poverty Line as of September. For those already struggling to afford water, the program works by gradually wiping away pre-September outstanding balances as long as residents keep up with monthly payments. A household with $1,000 in arrears, for instance, will see roughly $41.60 of that debt forgiven each month they pay on time—meaning the full balance vanishes within two years.

What makes the program surprisingly generous is its built-in flexibility. Customers can miss up to two monthly payments and remain enrolled; only after three missed payments are they removed. "There's help out there for people who are struggling," said Julie Mechling, Pittsburgh Water's director of customer service. "There are multiple opportunities for you to come to us and see what protections are available to you."

The program reflects an unusual form of mutual aid from a public utility. Pittsburgh Water notes that more than 95% of its customer base neither carries outstanding debt nor misses payments—meaning the smaller population of struggling households can benefit from the financial health of the broader community. By automating enrollment for those below the poverty threshold, the program removes barriers that often prevent eligible families from accessing help in the first place. It's a reminder that relief programs work best not when they require endless paperwork, but when they meet people where they are.
quick_facts: 4,300 Pittsburgh households automatically enrolled in September
24-month period to forgive all pre-September outstanding debt
Customers can miss up to 2 payments and stay enrolled
$1,000 example debt becomes $41.60 monthly forgiveness installments
Targets households below 200% of Federal Poverty Line
